positions.catalyst: A reported stabilization or re-acceleration of snack and beverage volumes and a consumer-staples re-rating off a 52-week low.
positions.invalidation: Continued structural volume decline in its core categories, or sustained margin compression from input and wage costs, would show that the de-rating was fundamental rather than cyclical.

positions.name: Berkshire Hathaway Class B
positions.thesis: The world thesis applied is that a diversified insurance-and-industrial conglomerate with a large float-based funding advantage and historically substantial cash is the natural late-cycle holding when the price of optionality is high and real rates are positive, because the conglomerate itself is a diversified value vehicle rather than a single-business bet; the packet shows it at 509.77 with a 12-month return of only 3.5% and a 52-week range of 465 to 529, so it has behaved with notably low volatility relative to the market and is near the middle of its range. The durable mechanism I can state is the insurance float and the breadth of operating businesses across rail, energy, manufacturing and consumer; the claim that its cash position is large is general background knowledge I cannot verify at the cutoff and I flag it as an assumption. The catalyst is deployment of capital at attractive prices in a dislocation or continued float-funded compounding; what would prove this wrong is a major insurance underwriting loss or a poor large acquisition; the 6% weight treats it as a lower-volatility equity core rather than a growth engine.
positions.catalyst: Deployment of accumulated capital into a market dislocation, continued float-funded compounding, or a re-rating of a low-volatility diversified compounder if growth stocks de-rate.
positions.invalidation: A large insurance underwriting or catastrophic-loss event, a badly priced major acquisition, or leadership transition missteps would prove this application of the thesis wrong.

positions.name: SPDR Gold Shares
positions.thesis: This is the direct application of the thesis that fiscal and geopolitical fragmentation keeps an inflation and confidence tail alive even as the base case is disinflation, so a monetary metal with no counterparty exposure deserves a small permanent sleeve; the packet shows it at 401.17 with a 12-month return of 19.1% and a 52-week range of 335.62 to 495.90, so it has already risen a long way and I hold 6% as insurance rather than as a momentum bet. The durable mechanism is gold's role as a reserve asset that responds to real rates, currency debasement concerns and geopolitical stress; the catalyst is any re-acceleration of inflation, fiscal stress, or a decline in real yields. What would prove this wrong is a sustained rise in real yields and a resolution of geopolitical and fiscal concerns, which would pressure the price; the 6% weight is calibrated so that even a 25% gold drawdown costs the portfolio about 1.5%, well within the low-risk objective.
positions.catalyst: A re-acceleration of inflation, a fiscal or geopolitical confidence shock, or a decline in real interest rates, any of which historically supports monetary-metal demand.
positions.invalidation: A sustained increase in real yields combined with credible fiscal consolidation and geopolitical de-escalation would remove the thesis and likely the premium in the price.

positions.name: Energy Select Sector SPDR
positions.thesis: The application is that disciplined global energy supply plus geopolitical fragmentation keeps commodity upside optionality valuable as inflation insurance, and that integrated energy equities currently generate strong cash returns while serving that hedge; the packet shows it at 64.31 with a 12-month return of 47.4% and a 52-week range of 41.68 to 65.93, meaning it is at the very top of its 52-week range, so the sizing at 3% reflects a real risk of buying late in a commodity cycle. The durable mechanism is capital discipline among producers and non-discretionary global energy demand; the catalyst is supply disruption or a stronger-than-expected global growth and inflation path. What would prove this wrong is a demand-driven commodity collapse or an OPEC+ production surge, both of which would hurt both the hedge value and the price; the 3% weight keeps this asymmetric hedge from becoming a speculative bet.
positions.catalyst: A supply disruption, renewed geopolitical escalation, or stronger global demand with continued producer capital discipline.
positions.invalidation: A global demand slump or a coordinated production surge that drives crude sharply lower would invalidate both the hedge value and the recent re-rating.

positions.name: iShares 1-3 Year Treasury Bond ETF
positions.thesis: This is the purest expression of the restrictive-real-rates thesis: if policy rates stay at least neutral, short-duration government paper earns a real coupon without taking the duration or credit risk that would hurt a low-risk book if inflation or growth surprises; the packet shows it at 81.24 with a 12-month return of 1.5% and a 52-week range of 79.92 to 81.84, a price path consistent with very small price volatility and with income being the dominant return source. The durable mechanism is the rollover of 1-3 year maturities at prevailing short rates; the catalyst is simply the passage of time plus any policy-rate support. What would prove this wrong is a sudden deflationary collapse that makes long duration far superior, or a fiscal-confidence crisis that hurts even short Treasuries; at 10% it is the largest single non-equity position because it is the least risky instrument in the packet.
positions.catalyst: Continued coupon accrual at policy rates and any flight to quality during a growth scare, which would support the price as well as the yield.
positions.invalidation: A severe deflationary event that makes long duration far more attractive, or a loss of confidence in US government paper, would prove the short-duration application wrong.

positions.name: iShares 7-10 Year Treasury Bond ETF
positions.thesis: The thesis applied is that a decelerating late-cycle economy with restrictive policy eventually gives way to softer growth, and intermediate Treasuries are the classic portfolio ballast that pays you to wait for that to happen; the packet shows it at 90.80 with a 12-month return of -2.7% and a 52-week range of 90.73 to 95.75, so it is essentially at its 52-week low and therefore provides that ballast at a price where a good deal of rate pain is already reflected. The durable mechanism is the duration premium and the negative equity correlation that Treasuries usually show in growth shocks; the catalyst is any confirmed economic slowdown or a Fed pivot toward easing. What would prove this wrong is a re-acceleration of inflation that pushes yields higher and cuts the price, or a fiscal supply shock; the 5% weight limits the duration exposure while still providing recession ballast.
positions.catalyst: Confirmed deceleration in growth and inflation, or a policy pivot toward lower rates, which would raise the price of intermediate-duration government bonds.
positions.invalidation: Renewed inflation above expectations, a Treasury supply or fiscal credibility shock, or an aggressive re-pricing of the long end would invalidate the ballast argument.

positions.name: iShares iBoxx USD Investment Grade Corporate Bond ETF
positions.thesis: The application is that if real rates stay restrictive but the economy merely slows rather than collapses, investment-grade corporate bonds deliver a higher coupon than Treasuries without reaching into equity-like risk, which is exactly the sweet spot for a low-risk 24-month objective; the packet shows it at 104.70 with a 12-month return of -2.2% and a 52-week range of 104.28 to 108.72, so it is near the bottom of its range and the price already reflects a good deal of rate pressure. The durable mechanism is corporate coupon carry with a spread that historically tightens when recession fears fade; the catalyst is spread compression in a soft-landing scenario. What would prove this wrong is a recession that pushes default and downgrade risk into the investment-grade tier and widens spreads sharply; the 5% weight, together with 15% in government fixed income and 16% cash, keeps credit risk modest and the drawdown estimate defensible.
positions.catalyst: Spread compression in a soft-landing scenario, or continued coupon income if spreads stay flat while Treasuries stabilize.
positions.invalidation: A hard recession that causes significant downgrades and spread widening in the investment-grade market would prove the application wrong and would raise realized drawdown.

pick.knowledgeLimitations: I can see only the packet's adjusted closing prices, 3-month and 12-month price returns and trailing 52-week highs and lows through 2026-09-18, which is about three and a half weeks before the reference timestamp, so any event after 2026-09-18 is invisible to me and could have changed the picture. I cannot verify any current valuation multiple, earnings figure, guidance, interest-rate level, credit spread, fund yield, expense ratio, fund holdings or news event, and I do not know the Fed funds rate or the current level of inflation at the cutoff; my theses about real rates and inflation are world views built on general knowledge and on what the cross-section of returns in the packet is consistent with, not on data I have confirmed. I am assuming standard sector classifications (for example that XLP.US holds consumer staples and XLU.US holds regulated utilities), that these ETFs track their usual indices, and that gold and energy behave as partial inflation hedges, all of which could be wrong. Anything about company-specific fundamentals — PEP.US's volume trends, BRK-B.US's cash pile, healthcare policy, oil supply agreements — is either general background knowledge that may be stale or an explicit assumption, and I flag it as such rather than presenting it as verified fact.

strategies.riskRationale: The book keeps only about 58% of capital in equity beta, spread across a broad index, a value tilt, a dividend-quality tilt and three defensive sectors, so no single company or theme can drive the outcome; roughly 20% sits in short and intermediate investment-grade fixed income and 16% in cash, which together with a 6% gold sleeve is intended to compress peak-to-trough decline toward the low-teens rather than the roughly 25-35% an all-equity book would suffer in a recession or multiple-compression episode. A 24-month horizon is long enough for defensive cash-flow re-rating and coupon carry to matter, but short enough that a single policy or earnings shock can dominate the path, so the sizing favors preservation over maximizing the forecast return.

pick.risks: The main risks are that the hard-asset and financial sleeves are both correlated to nominal growth and would draw down together in a recession; the dislocated-quality sleeve could stay cheap if the causes of those 20-56% drawdowns are structural rather than cyclical, which I cannot verify; the 4% crypto sleeve is far more volatile than the rest of the book; energy concentration is meaningful (XOM.US, CVX.US, SLB.US and COP.US together are 18%), so an oil price collapse would hit the book hard; and commodity prices shown in the packet are already up 45-105% over 12 months, so mean reversion from these levels is a real downside path. Estimated peak-to-trough maximum drawdown over the target period is 20% (roughly 25-28% in a recession scenario and roughly 12-15% if only the value sleeve lags), which fits a medium objective that accepts meaningful fluctuation but does not rely on one speculative outcome.

theses.title: Hard-asset and power supercycle
theses.worldView: Over the 24 months to October 2028 I expect structural underinvestment in energy, metals and electrical infrastructure, combined with AI data-center electricity demand, grid buildout and reshoring capital expenditure, to keep real commodity prices and upstream cash flows elevated; the claim is falsified if the broad commodity complex tracked in the packet (DBC.US, USO.US, GLD.US, SLV.US) round-trips below its trailing 52-week lows and energy and mining margins compress for four consecutive quarters without a demand shock.
theses.portfolioExpression: About 39% of capital in oil majors and oilfield services, a copper producer, gold and silver exposures, a diversified commodity basket, and electrical and cooling equipment suppliers, with individual weights of 2-6% so that no single commodity, company or project decides the result.

theses.title: Quality dislocation and mean reversion
theses.worldView: The packet shows record dispersion (NKE.US, INTU.US, ZTS.US, BSX.US, ORCL.US, PEP.US and MCD.US are down 20-56% over 12 months or sit at their 52-week lows while energy and AI hardware compounded), and I assume much of that gap prices temporary volume, inventory, traffic and expectation noise as permanent franchise impairment, so over 24 months normalized volumes, margins and capital returns should re-rate these businesses; the claim is falsified if unit volumes and margins keep deteriorating for four or more additional quarters or if these franchises keep losing share structurally.
theses.portfolioExpression: About 28% of capital in consumer staples and franchised restaurants at or exactly at their 52-week lows, a home improvement retailer, and durable software, animal-health and medtech franchises sold down 20-56%, each held at 2-4% so the sleeve tolerates further mean-reversion delays.

theses.title: Capital markets and credit upcycle
theses.worldView: Nominal growth, elevated asset prices, heavy issuance and a recovering M&A pipeline keep fee income, underwriting, trading and net interest income strong for scaled financial institutions and exchanges through 2028 while credit costs stay contained; the claim is falsified by a sharp rise in charge-offs, sustained net interest margin compression, or a freeze in issuance and deal activity.
theses.portfolioExpression: About 19% of capital in a diversified insurance and industrial conglomerate, two large universal banks, a leading investment bank, and a derivatives exchange whose volumes benefit from the same volatile, commodity-rich regime this book is betting on.

theses.title: Monetary debasement hedge
theses.worldView: Large fiscal deficits and real-asset inflation keep a scarce, liquid, non-sovereign monetary asset useful as a small hedge against fiat debasement, and the sharp last-quarter rebounds in the packet (BTC-USD.CC +28% over 3 months, ETH-USD.CC +54%) suggest the post-correction phase of that cycle; the claim is falsified by sustained outflows from regulated spot vehicles, a protocol-level failure, or a coordinated regulatory shutdown in major markets.
theses.portfolioExpression: A capped 4% sleeve split between the largest proof-of-work monetary network and the largest programmable settlement network, sized so that a 70% drawdown in the sleeve costs the whole portfolio only about 2.8%.

theses.title: Cash as dry powder
theses.worldView: With several segments near their 52-week highs and many quality names at their lows, I assume valuation dispersion and macro uncertainty stay high enough that a 10% cash reserve improves resilience and becomes an option on a later dislocation; the claim is falsified if the market grinds higher for 24 months without a 10% correction, in which case the 0% cash return is an explicit opportunity cost.
theses.portfolioExpression: A 10% cashWeight held uninvested, explicitly expressed as a view that patience has value in a market where winners and losers are priced so far apart, and as the ballast that keeps a cyclical and crypto-tinged book inside a medium risk profile.

pick.thesis: The book is built on four linked world views: a hard-asset and power buildout that keeps commodity cash flows strong (39%), a market that has over-punished durable franchises at or near 52-week lows (28%), a capital-markets and credit environment that rewards scaled financial intermediaries (19%), and a small monetary-debasement hedge in spot crypto (4%), with 10% cash as deliberate patience. The tension between theses is explicit: the hard-asset sleeve benefits if inflation and nominal growth stay hot, while the dislocated-quality sleeve benefits if consumer volumes and margins normalize as cost pressures ease; the weights resolve this by keeping each sleeve under 40% and each name under 6%, so being partly wrong on one world view does not break the portfolio.

forecasts.reason: A 13% total return over 24 months is plausible if oil and metals stay firm rather than collapse from the high levels shown in the packet, consumer volumes and margins in the dislocated-quality sleeve stabilize and re-rate at least partway back toward their prior ranges, credit costs stay contained so the financials sleeve keeps earning, and the crypto sleeve recovers moderately instead of falling further; this is an assumption-based central estimate with wide error bars, and a recession, an oil price crash, or structural rather than cyclical causes behind the 20-56% drawdowns I bought into would push realized returns well below it, while continued commodity strength and broad multiple expansion could exceed it.

positions.name: Exxon Mobil
positions.thesis: An integrated oil major with low-cost upstream growth and large refining and chemicals exposure is the cleanest listed expression of my view that underinvestment keeps real crude prices elevated through 2028; the packet shows it at 163.54 near its 52-week high of 169.32 with +46% over 12 months, so the market is pricing a firm cycle rather than a distressed one, and my assumption (not a verified figure) is that its cash flow breakevens sit far below the oil prices implied by USO.US more than doubling off its 52-week low. The durable mechanism is multi-decade low-cost resource life plus integrated downstream margin capture.
positions.catalyst: Continued buyback and dividend increases funded by free cash flow, plus volume growth from low-cost Permian and international developments, would unlock the value as the hard-asset cycle persists.
positions.invalidation: A sustained collapse in crude that takes USO.US back below its 52-week low of 66.17, or four straight quarters of upstream and refining margin compression, would invalidate both the world thesis and this application, and at 6% it is sized so that this outcome costs the portfolio roughly 2-3%.

positions.name: Chevron
positions.thesis: A second integrated major expresses the same hard-asset view with different assets and a different cost curve, which is why I hold two majors rather than concentrating in one; the packet shows +36% over 12 months and a price of 209.51 within 4% of its 52-week high of 217.77, and my assumption is that the balance sheet and buyback capacity are intact. The mechanism is long-life Permian and international projects with capital discipline.
positions.catalyst: Free cash flow conversion at firm commodity prices, sustained buybacks and portfolio high-grading would unlock the value.
positions.invalidation: If oil and gas prices fall far enough that integrated majors cut buybacks and dividends, or if the company's project execution visibly lags peers, this application fails; the 5% weight keeps a commodity setback within the medium risk profile.

positions.name: SLB (Schlumberger)
positions.thesis: Oilfield services express the same world view with operating leverage: if upstream capital expenditure stays elevated because producers must replace depleted barrels, service pricing and international and offshore project work benefit more than the producers themselves; the packet shows +51% over 12 months with the price at 51.12 still below its 52-week high of 59.79, so I am paying for the cycle but not its peak. The mechanism is multi-year international and offshore project backlog with high incremental margins.
positions.catalyst: A rising international and offshore rig count, service pricing increases and offshore final investment decisions converting into backlog would unlock the value.
positions.invalidation: A downturn in producer capital spending, visible as falling service revenue and pricing, would invalidate the application; at 4% the position is a deliberate but limited leverage bet on the same thesis.

positions.name: ConocoPhillips
positions.thesis: A pure-play exploration and production company with a low-cost shale and liquefied natural gas portfolio expresses the view that replacement barrels are scarce and expensive to find; the packet shows +45% over 12 months at 131.83 against a 52-week high of 141.22, and my assumption is that the portfolio sits at the low end of the industry cost curve. The mechanism is short-cycle shale flexibility plus long-life international volumes.
positions.catalyst: Capital returns through buybacks and dividends alongside low-cost volume growth while commodity prices hold would unlock the value.
positions.invalidation: Sustained sub-breakeven commodity prices or a capital allocation mistake such as overpaying for acquisitions would invalidate it; 3% reflects higher single-commodity price sensitivity than the majors.

positions.name: Freeport-McMoRan
positions.thesis: Copper is the physical bottleneck of electrification, grid expansion, AI data-center power and electric drivetrains, and a large low-cost miner expresses that world view with torque; the packet shows +60% over 12 months at 71.54 versus a 52-week high of 79.91. The durable mechanism is long-life tier-one ore bodies with long permitting lead times that constrain new supply.
positions.catalyst: Grid, electrification and AI data-center copper demand meeting a slow supply response, lifting realized copper prices and free cash flow, would unlock the value.
positions.invalidation: If refined copper inventories build and prices fall back toward the lows of the sector range while energy and construction demand weakens, the thesis is wrong for this holding; 4% balances strong leverage to the theme against mine-level execution and political risk.

positions.name: Newmont
positions.thesis: Gold mining expresses the monetary side of the hard-asset view: if deficits and real-asset inflation persist and official-sector demand for gold continues (a known trend in my training data that I assume has not reversed), then miners convert high gold prices into free cash flow with cost discipline; the packet shows +58% over 12 months at 123.41 versus a 52-week high of 134.86, with GLD.US itself up 19%. The mechanism is operating leverage to the gold price plus portfolio simplification.
positions.catalyst: Margin expansion as the gold price grows faster than mining costs, plus buybacks and asset high-grading, would unlock the value.
positions.invalidation: A sustained decline in gold toward the lows of the sector range combined with renewed cost inflation would invalidate this application; 3% reflects mining-specific execution and jurisdiction risk.

positions.name: SPDR Gold Shares
positions.thesis: A physically backed gold vehicle expresses the view that real assets retain monetary relevance when fiscal deficits and inflation are persistent; the packet shows it at 401.17 with a 52-week high of 495.90 and +19% over 12 months, so I am buying a partially retraced rather than an extended gold move. The mechanism is portfolio-level inflation and currency debasement hedging with low equity correlation.
positions.catalyst: Continued central bank and investor allocation to real stores of value, and fiscal deficits that keep real-asset inflation elevated, would unlock the value.
positions.invalidation: If real interest rates rise enough to make non-yielding gold unattractive and gold breaks materially below its 52-week low of 335.62, the thesis fails; 3% is sized as a hedge rather than a return engine.

positions.name: iShares Silver Trust
positions.thesis: Silver expresses the same hard-asset view with an industrial edge, since solar, electronics and grid hardware consume a large share of supply while monetary demand adds a second buyer; the packet shows +59% over 12 months at 59.93 against a 52-week high of 105.60, meaning the position is still roughly 43% below its own yearly peak. The mechanism is a supply deficit driven by industrial offtake plus monetary hedging.
positions.catalyst: Accelerating photovoltaic, electronics and grid-hardware demand creating a physical silver supply deficit would unlock the value.
positions.invalidation: A manufacturing recession that collapses industrial metal demand, or a repeat of the sharp mean reversion implied by the gap to the 52-week high, would invalidate the sizing rationale; 2% keeps this volatile instrument small.

positions.name: Invesco DB Commodity Index Tracking Fund
positions.thesis: A diversified commodity basket expresses the hard-asset view at the level of the regime rather than one commodity or company, which reduces single-story risk inside the sleeve; the packet shows +51% over 12 months at 32.93 versus a 52-week high of 33.68. The mechanism is broad exposure to energy, metals and agriculture that benefits when real asset prices stay elevated.
positions.catalyst: Continued supply underinvestment across energy, metals and agriculture keeping broad real-asset prices elevated would unlock the value.
positions.invalidation: If the broad commodity complex round-trips below its 52-week low of 21.35, the world thesis for this sleeve is falsified; 2% is a diversifier weight, not a directional concentration.

positions.name: Eaton
positions.thesis: Electrical equipment is the picks-and-shovels expression of the power buildout: every additional gigawatt of data center and grid load requires switchgear, transformers, busway and power distribution where lead times are long and pricing has held; the packet shows +18% over 12 months at 424.77 versus a 52-week high of 459.96. The mechanism is electrical content per unit of infrastructure rising while capacity is constrained.
positions.catalyst: Data center and utility capital spending converting electrical equipment backlog into revenue and margin would unlock the value.
positions.invalidation: A visible pause in data-center and utility capital spending, or an electrical equipment capacity glut, would invalidate this application; 4% balances the theme's strength against the fact that the market has already rewarded it.

positions.name: Carrier Global
positions.thesis: Cooling and thermal management for data centers and buildings is a second-order way to express the same power and compute buildout at a price that has not been rewarded; the packet shows it down 9.9% over 12 months at 53.88 versus a 52-week low of 49.79 and a 52-week high of 75.73. The mechanism is that heat rejection is a hard physical constraint on compute density.
positions.catalyst: Data center cooling orders plus a recovery in replacement and construction demand would unlock the value.
positions.invalidation: If construction and renovation activity keep weakening and data-center cooling orders stall, the dislocation is not a bargain; 3% treats it as a reasonably priced expression of a theme priced elsewhere at a premium.

positions.name: PepsiCo
positions.thesis: A global snacks and beverages franchise is exactly at its 52-week low of 129.75 in the packet, down 4.4% over 12 months and 7.7% over 3 months, which is the kind of price dislocation my second thesis targets; my assumption is that weak volumes and traffic reflect a squeezed consumer and a cost cycle rather than a permanent loss of brand power or shelf presence. The mechanism is pricing power, a direct-store-delivery and distribution moat, and dividend and buyback support.
positions.catalyst: Volume stabilization and then recovery as input-cost comparisons ease, with pricing holding, would unlock the value.
positions.invalidation: If organic volumes keep declining for four or more additional quarters and margins stay below prior peaks, the franchise is being re-rated for structural reasons and the thesis is wrong; 4% is the largest weight in the sleeve because the cash flows are the least cyclical there.

positions.name: McDonald's
positions.thesis: The stock sits exactly at its 52-week low of 248.24 and is down 16.5% over 12 months, and I apply the same world view: a franchised royalty stream with global brand recognition is being priced as if low-income traffic weakness is permanent. The mechanism is asset-light franchising that converts sales into high-margin royalty and rent income with cost support from scale.
positions.catalyst: A traffic recovery led by value menus and easier input-cost comparisons, alongside international unit growth, would unlock the value.
positions.invalidation: Sustained negative same-store sales across all regions for several more quarters would show the weakness is structural; 3% reflects that the brand is durable but the consumer backdrop is genuinely uncertain.

positions.name: Nike
positions.thesis: The stock is exactly at its 52-week low of 35.51 and down 49.3% over 12 months, the single largest dislocation in the consumer set, and my assumption (unverifiable from the packet) is that inventory, wholesale channel reset and product-cycle noise are being priced as permanent impairment of the world's largest athletic brand. The mechanism is brand pricing power, global distribution and marketing scale.
positions.catalyst: A renewed product innovation cycle and normalized wholesale inventory restoring brand momentum would unlock the value.
positions.invalidation: If market share keeps migrating to competitors for four or more additional quarters despite a new product pipeline, this is franchise decay and not a bargain; 3% reflects high idiosyncratic uncertainty, which is why it is not larger.

positions.name: Yum Brands
positions.thesis: A globally franchised restaurant platform trades at 137.99 against a 52-week low of 135.58 and is down 5.1% over 12 months, so I am buying the same consumer-traffic dislocation at a smaller price, with a larger share of international and emerging-market growth. The mechanism is an asset-light royalty model with unit economics that franchisees keep expanding.
positions.catalyst: International unit growth and digital sales-mix improvement driving same-store sales would unlock the value.
positions.invalidation: A multi-year halt in unit development or sustained negative same-store sales would invalidate the application; 2% is a satellite weight inside the dislocation sleeve.

positions.name: Lowe's
positions.thesis: The stock sits at its 52-week low of 192.49 and is down 26.7% over 12 months, and I apply the thesis through the housing and repair cycle: my assumption is that weak turnover and big-ticket remodeling deferral are cyclical and that aging housing stock sustains long-run repair demand. The mechanism is a scaled home improvement duopoly with strong free cash flow and buybacks.
positions.catalyst: A recovery in housing turnover and repair spending as financing conditions and rate expectations ease would unlock the value.
positions.invalidation: If housing turnover and repair spending keep falling for two more years, or if the company loses share structurally to online rivals, the thesis fails; 2.5% reflects genuine sensitivity to the rate and housing cycle.

positions.name: Oracle
positions.thesis: The packet shows a rare mega-cap dislocation: down 50.5% over 12 months at 147.61 against a 52-week high of 324.45, yet still above its 52-week low of 114.99, and I explicitly cannot verify from my knowledge what caused it; my assumption is expectation and financing compression around an AI capital spending cycle rather than destruction of the database and cloud franchise. The mechanism is mission-critical database and enterprise application lock-in with long contracts.
positions.catalyst: Cloud backlog converting into recognized revenue and margins, and clearer disclosure on the returns to AI capital spending, would unlock the value.
positions.invalidation: If cloud bookings keep deteriorating, margins compress structurally, or balance sheet strain from capital spending becomes clear, the drawdown is fundamental and this application is wrong; 2.5% is deliberately small given my inability to verify the cause of the fall.

positions.name: Zoetis
positions.thesis: The stock is essentially at its 52-week low of 71.36 (price 71.40) and down 50.5% over 12 months, and I apply the thesis through demographics: pet ownership and companion-animal health spending are durable in my world view while channel destocking and clinic traffic noise are not. positions.name: Bitcoin spot

positions.invalidation: Sustained outflows from regulated spot vehicles, a protocol-level failure, or a coordinated regulatory shutdown in major markets would invalidate the thesis; 2.5% is sized so that even a 70% crash costs the portfolio only about 1.8%.

positions.invalidation: Loss of developer and fee activity to competing networks, or the same regulatory and structural risks as the first asset, would invalidate it; 1.5% keeps the more volatile of the two clearly subordinate.

pick.knowledgeLimitations: My training data ends well before the packet's 2026-09-18 cutoff, so I cannot verify current earnings, valuation multiples, interest rates, index levels, news, or the causes of the large price moves shown (for example why ORCL.US, BSX.US, ZTS.US, INTU.US or NFLX.US fell 20-56%, or why MU.US, MRNA.US and INTC.US rose several hundred percent); the packet supplies only prices, returns and 52-week ranges, so value here means price dislocation combined with durable business quality rather than a verified low multiple or margin of safety from fundamentals. Some absolute price levels in the packet differ sharply from my memory of earlier levels for the same names, implying corporate actions such as splits or adjustments that I cannot confirm, so I rely on the packet's relative returns and ranges rather than remembered price history. All business descriptions come from general public knowledge before my cutoff and may be stale, and every catalyst or mechanism I name is an assumption rather than a verified current fact.

strategies.riskRationale: Medium risk means balancing upside with resilience over a full two years: 90% of capital is invested across 29 positions and four explicit theses, no single name exceeds 6%, the crypto sleeve is capped at 4% so it cannot drive the outcome, the book is deliberately barbelled between hard assets and deeply dislocated quality franchises whose return drivers are only partially correlated, and 10% cash cushions drawdowns and preserves optionality in a packet that shows record dispersion between 52-week winners and losers.

pick.risks: The dominant risks are a hard landing in which AI capital spending is cut and the power and software legs fall together, a commodity mean reversion that punishes XOM.US, FCX.US and NEM.US after twelve-month gains of 46% to 60%, a further leg down in crypto that drives BTC below its 52-week low near 58,559, and company-specific shocks such as balance-sheet stress at the heavily de-rated ORCL.US or regulatory and delisting pressure on PDD.US and SE.US; cross-correlations are meaningful because the software, power, crypto and emerging-market legs are all equity-market risk factors that tend to draw down simultaneously during liquidity events, so a 45% peak-to-trough decline is a realistic central risk estimate rather than a tail scenario.

theses.title: Electricity, not chips, is the AI bottleneck
theses.worldView: Through 2028 the binding constraint on artificial-intelligence and data-center deployment in the United States is electricity generation, transmission and grid equipment rather than semiconductors, so nominal spending on power generation and electrical equipment grows faster than chip spending and grid interconnection queues remain multi-year long.
theses.portfolioExpression: This book overweights gas-turbine, electrical-equipment and nuclear-generation equities such as GEV.US, ETN.US and CEG.US, several of which sit 8% to 37% below their 52-week highs, and holds no semiconductor or memory exposure despite those sectors having compounded 150% to 500% over the past twelve months.

theses.title: De-rated cash-flow software re-rates
theses.worldView: The 2026 equity market over-dispersed returns toward memory and hardware winners and away from durable recurring-revenue software franchises, so over the next 24 months free-cash-flow and earnings growth at the de-rated franchises pushes their multiples back toward their own history instead of toward permanent decline.
theses.portfolioExpression: The portfolio holds cash-generative software franchises priced roughly 28% to 56% below their 52-week highs, including ORCL.US, ADBE.US, INTU.US and SPOT.US, as a concentrated bet that the market's implied growth rates are too pessimistic.

theses.title: Fiscal dominance keeps real assets expensive
theses.worldView: Large US fiscal deficits, deglobalization and industrial policy keep inflation and commodity real prices structurally elevated through 2028, so claims on scarce real assets such as gold, silver, copper and hydrocarbons preserve purchasing power better than long-duration nominal bonds.
theses.portfolioExpression: The book expresses this through GLD.US and SLV.US physical metal trusts plus NEM.US, FCX.US and XOM.US producers, while deliberately holding no government bond ETFs such as AGG.US or TLT.US, which show flat to negative twelve-month returns in the frozen snapshot.

theses.title: Crypto drawdown is cyclical, not terminal
theses.worldView: Institutional and corporate adoption of decentralized monetary and smart-contract networks continues along a multi-year S-curve, so the 2026 drawdown visible in the snapshot, with BTC down 29.8%, ETH down 41.1% and SOL down 53.5% over twelve months, is a cyclical bear inside an adoption trend and major network capitalizations and usage exceed their 2025 highs by late 2028.
theses.portfolioExpression: The portfolio holds spot BTC-USD.CC, ETH-USD.CC and a small SOL-USD.CC position at prices 35% to 54% below their 52-week highs as an explicitly contrarian cycle-trough expression with an 18% combined weight.

theses.title: Emerging-market digital consumption compounds
theses.worldView: Middle-class digital consumption, e-commerce formalization and fintech adoption in Latin America and Southeast Asia keep compounding through 2028, so local platform leaders whose share prices imply stagnation grow faster than mature US consumer businesses.
theses.portfolioExpression: The book holds MELI.US, SE.US and a small PDD.US position at 27% to 47% below their 52-week highs as the direct expression of emerging-market consumer digitalization.

pick.thesis: This is a concentrated, contrarian 24-month book built on five linked world views: the AI buildout migrates its spending bottleneck from chips to power; the market's 2026 return dispersion has underpriced cash-flow software; fiscal dominance keeps scarce real assets valuable; the crypto adoption cycle is near a cyclical trough rather than a terminal decline; and emerging-market digital consumption compounds beneath de-rated platform valuations. The main internal tension is that the software, power and crypto legs are pro-risk and pro-AI-capex while the hard-asset leg is an inflation and debasement hedge that benefits if nominal growth and the dollar weaken; the roughly 40% combined weight in power and software is balanced by 26% in hard assets, 18% in crypto and 11% in emerging-market platforms so that no single macro outcome dominates the book, and the 5% cash weight reflects a deliberately small buffer in a regime where valuations cannot be verified from the frozen packet.

forecasts.reason: A 25% total return over 24 months is plausible if the AI power-spending cycle persists while electricity remains scarce, the de-rated software franchises re-rate as free cash flow grows, hard assets hold their inflation hedge as deficits continue, crypto adoption resumes a cyclical recovery toward 2028 highs, and emerging-market consumer platforms stabilize; the honest uncertainty band is very wide, plausibly from minus 30% to plus 80% given the concentration and the 45% drawdown risk, and the forecast would fail if AI capex contracts, oil mean-reverts sharply, or the crypto cycle extends further downward instead of recovering.

theses.title: Short duration is the one-month anchor.

theses.portfolioExpression: I express this view with 60% cash and 20% SHY.US, an ETF of short-maturity U.S. Treasury exposure, accepting zero cash return and limited upside in exchange for lower rate and equity sensitivity over a one-month holding period.

theses.title: Essential demand and diversification cushion uneven growth.
theses.worldView: If the next month brings uneven growth rather than a synchronized expansion, spending on everyday necessities and diversified financially resilient businesses should experience a smaller earnings shock than speculative or highly cyclical exposures; the thesis is falsified by a severe broad demand contraction or a sustained cyclical risk-on surge.
theses.portfolioExpression: I apply this view with small allocations to XLP.US and BRK-B.US, using essential-demand characteristics and business diversification as equity satellites rather than making them the portfolio's primary risk.

theses.title: Real assets hedge nominal-regime surprises.
theses.worldView: If inflation expectations, fiscal confidence or geopolitical risk deteriorate over the month, gold can diversify nominal bonds and equities; this thesis is falsified if real yields rise, disinflation persists and risk appetite remains strong enough for gold to underperform.
